title: Tokyo's Shinjuku Station Tests Trash Can Robots
paragraphs: Finding a trash can in Japan can be difficult. In fact, a 2025 survey found that it was the most common problem for visitors to Japan.
But at one of Tokyo's busiest train stations, you may no longer have to look for one — because the trash can could come looking for you!
JR East has started testing mobile trash can robots at Shinjuku Station. The trial began on September 8 and will run until November 20.
The robots run from Monday to Friday between 10 a.m. and 5 p.m.

The small robots, made by US company Cartken, move automatically around part of the station's underground area, collecting general trash and plastic bottles from passengers. And when they're full, they make their way back to the station's trash collection area.
And fittingly for a train station, they even look a little like trains! Each robot has large cartoon eyes, the colors of JR train lines and pictures of Shinjukuma, Shinjuku Station's bear mascot.
But the trial is testing more than just a high-tech trash can. JR East also wants to see if the robots can move safely through the station's large crowds without getting in the way.
Online, however, people were more worried about something else: whether the robots would be able to find their way around Shinjuku Station at all.
Shinjuku Station is famously difficult to get around, and one of the top Reddit comments about the robot simply said: "It will get lost."
Another Instagram user joked that the robot's next upgrade should be helping people find their way out of the station.
But at least for now, finding a trash can at Shinjuku Station should be a little easier!
